name: authority-scope-inventory
objective: Establish one current BB Captain-only execution boundary and invalidate stale package assumptions before product writes.
truthOwner: Current task and governance/Product Truth define scope; Identity/Workforce own access/profile truth, DSH owns Captain operational truth, WLT owns financial truth.

tasks.objective: Rebaseline the Captain impact graph on current BB
tasks.currentProblem: The previous package is bound to abbas and an old SHA, while BB contains material Captain/Identity/Workforce/DSH/mobile/finance/test changes and the current package schema changed.
tasks.requiredChange: Re-resolve BB, reconcile concurrent movement, use current authority/Product Truth/source to classify every direct Captain path and replace stale package evidence without touching product/runtime code in this foundation task.
tasks.targetState: The package names the current branch/SHA, current schema, current implemented behavior, current open verification risks and only directly affected surfaces.
tasks.action: Re-resolve BB; inspect the live prompting/framework/authority/Product Truth and Captain implementation paths; compare stale assumptions; update only this existing package; run strict validation when shell is available.
mustNotChange: Do not create another app-captain package.
Do not change product/runtime/governance code while performing the package rebaseline.
Do not treat ArchPulse output or planning registries as Product Truth.
acceptanceCriteria: Manifest and all package references are current for BB and current validator schema.
Stale claims about empty architecture or missing Captain commission readback are removed.
Every related surface/control-panel section has evidence-backed coverage and every exclusion has a reopen trigger.
tasks.rollback: Revert only the package rebaseline commit; never revert concurrent product fixes or rewrite branch history.
tasks.commitBoundary: One package-only U001 bookkeeping update; product implementation commits belong to later units.

tasks.currentProblem: Shared DSH/WLT infrastructure can cause scope bleed into app-field, catalogs, marketing, analytics, dashboard, generic login or unrelated finance.
tasks.requiredChange: Treat COVERAGE exclusions as hard boundaries and reopen them only when current code/Product Truth proves a Captain-caused shared dependency before a write.
tasks.targetState: Later units touch only Captain truth owners and directly affected consumers; unrelated product domains remain unchanged.
tasks.action: Before each later-unit write, map proposed paths to a RELATED coverage entry; if a new shared consumer is discovered, update evidence/reopen trigger first rather than broad-scanning or editing by proximity.
mustNotChange: Do not implement app-field behavior merely because representative finance code is generic.
Do not import customer-address/catalog/marketing/dashboard work into Captain execution.
Do not edit all consumers of a shared folder unless the changed contract actually affects them.
acceptanceCriteria: Every write in later units maps to a Captain-related coverage entry.
No excluded section is modified without prior evidence-backed reclassification.
Shared changes trigger verification of actual consumers without importing unrelated product scope.
tasks.rollback: Revert only the offending package/scope edit and restore the last evidence-backed Captain boundary.
tasks.commitBoundary: Scope-boundary changes are package bookkeeping and must be committed separately from product fixes.
